'''Benedikt Hallgrimsson''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FCAHS}} (born in 1967) is an Icelandic-Canadian biological anthropologist and evolutionary biologist. He is a Full Professor at the [[University of Calgary]]'s [[Cumming School of Medicine]] and scientific director of the Alberta Children's Hospital Research Institute. Hallgrimsson studies birth defects and the developmental genetics of anatomical variation.

==Early life and education==
Hallgrimsson was born in 1967<ref>{{cite web |title=Hallgrimsson, Benedikt 1967- |url=https://viaf.org/en/viaf/12588442 |publisher=VIAF |access-date=May 2, 2025}}</ref> in [[Reykjavík]], Iceland.<ref name="x">{{cite web |title=Hallgrímsson Lab: People |url=https://cumming.ucalgary.ca/lab/morpho/personnel |publisher=University of Calgary |access-date=May 2, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241012103358/https://cumming.ucalgary.ca/lab/morpho/personnel |archive-date=October 12, 2024}}</ref> After completing his [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in anthropology from the [[University of Alberta]] in 1989, he enrolled at the [[University of Chicago]] for his [[Master's degree]] and PhD.<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Dr. Benedikt Hallgrimsson |url=https://profiles.ucalgary.ca/benedikt-hallgrimsson |publisher=University of Calgary |access-date=May 2, 2025}}</ref> As a graduate student at the University of Chicago, Hallgrimsson also accepted a Graduate Student Fellowship at the [[National Museum of Natural History]] in 1993 and became an Instructor of Anatomy at the [[University of Puerto Rico]].<ref name="Haines">{{cite journal |last1=Haines |first1=Duane E. |title=AAA award winners |journal=[[The Anatomical Record]] |date=June 15, 2001 |volume=265 |issue=3 |pages=123–126 |doi=10.1002/ar.1131 |pmid=11458324 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ar.1131 |access-date=May 2, 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
Upon receiving his PhD in 1995, Hallgrimsson became an assistant professor of anatomy at the University of Puerto Rico. While he was promoted to associate professor in 1998, he only remained at the institution until 2000.<ref name="Haines"/> Hallgrimsson then joined the [[University of Calgary]]'s (U of C) Department of Cell Biology and Anatomy. As the assistant dean for undergraduate science education, Hallgrimsson co-developed and directed U of C's Bachelor of Health Sciences program.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Heyman |first1=David |title=New U of C degree program targets budding scientists |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/calgary-herald-new-u-of-c-degree-program/171587908/ |access-date=May 3, 2025 |publisher=Calgary Herald |date=March 31, 2003|via=newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=U of C: Program popular |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/calgary-herald-u-of-c-program-popular/171589971/ |access-date=May 3, 2025 |publisher=Calgary Herald |date=February 26, 2003|via=newspapers.com}}</ref> Hallgrimsson was the 2001 recipient of the Basmajian/Lippincott Williams & Wilkins Award for his "demonstrated commitment to excellence in teaching in the anatomical sciences."<ref name="Haines"/>

In 2018, Hallgrimsson was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=2018 AAAS Fellows approved by the AAAS Council |journal=Science |date=November 30, 2018 |volume=362 |issue=6418 |pages=1010–1013 |doi=10.1126/science.362.6418.101 |doi-broken-date=1 July 2025 |url=https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/science.362.6418.1010 |access-date=May 3, 2025}}</ref> He was also appointed the Scientific Director for Basic Science at the Alberta Children's Hospital Research Institute (ACHRI).<ref>{{cite web |title=Alberta Children's Hospital Research Institute Newsletter |url=https://research4kids.ucalgary.ca/sites/default/files/teams/6/newsletters/dec.-10-2018-achri-newsletter.pdf |publisher=Alberta Children's Hospital Research Institute |access-date=May 3, 2025 |date=December 10, 2018}}</ref> During the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Hallgrimsson co-led UCalgary's COVID-19 genomics research with Francois Bernier. Together, they tracked the spread and evolution of the virus to inform vaccine development.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McCoy |first1=Heath |title=Primates, Genomics and Ecology Lab takes on COVID-19 |url=https://ucalgary.ca/news/primates-genomics-and-ecology-lab-takes-covid-19 |publisher=University of Calgary |access-date=May 3, 2025 |date=May 26, 2020}}</ref> He also collaborated on a research project that aimed to use facial recognition software to develop better respirator options for children.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Quantitative analysis of facial shape in children to support respirator design |journal=Applied Ergonomics |date=October 24, 2024 |doi=10.1016/j.apergo.2024.104375 |pmid=39454317 |last1=Nemeth |first1=C. |last2=Hoskens |first2=H. |last3=Wilson |first3=G. |last4=Jones |first4=M. |last5=Dipietrantonio |first5=J. |last6=Salami |first6=B. |last7=Harnish |first7=D. |last8=Claes |first8=P. |last9=Weinberg |first9=S. M. |last10=Shriver |first10=M. D. |last11=Hallgrímsson |first11=B. |volume=122 |article-number=104375 }}</ref> In recognition of his academic accomplishments, Hallgrimsson was elected a Fellow of the [[Canadian Academy of Health Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tibbetts |first1=Melanie |title=Eight University of Calgary researchers inducted into prestigious Canadian Academy of Health Sciences |url=https://cumming.ucalgary.ca/news/eight-university-calgary-researchers-inducted-prestigious-canadian-academy-health-sciences |publisher=University of Calgary |access-date=May 3, 2025 |date=September 28, 2020}}</ref>  In 2022, Hallgrimsson was named Deputy Director of the ACHRI.<ref name="director">{{cite web |title=Director Update |url=https://research4kids.ucalgary.ca/sites/default/files/teams/6/newsletters/ACHRI%20Newsletter%20January%2017%2C%202022.pdf |publisher=Alberta Children's Hospital Research Institute |access-date=May 3, 2025 |date=January 17, 2022}}</ref> While in this role, Hallgrimsson co-developed a 3D facial imaging computer program that could identify rare genetic diseases in children.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cyperling |first1=Marta |last2=Coates |first2=Cody |title=Researchers use 3D imaging, machine learning to identify rare genetic diseases in children |url=https://ucalgary.ca/news/researchers-use-3d-imaging-machine-learning-identify-rare-genetic-diseases-children |publisher=University of Calgary |access-date=May 3, 2025 |date=October 22, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=3D Facial Scans Could Speed Diagnoses for Children with Rare Genetic Diseases |url=https://news.cuanschutz.edu/medicine/3d-facial-scans |publisher=University of Colorado |access-date=May 3, 2025 |date=June 4, 2020}}</ref>
